response.answer:
Yes. The **Master of Engineering in Building Science** is available to international applicants **through the full-time option only**. The part-time option is not available to international applicants.

Important details:

- A valid **BCIT study permit** is required before starting the full-time program.
- The **September 2026 full-time intake is closed**.
- Applications for the **September 2027 intake open October 1, 2026**.
- Admission is competitive and requires meeting the program’s English, academic, mathematics, documentation, and reference requirements.

Program details: https://www.bcit.ca/programs/building-science-master-of-engineering-full-time-part-time-m120meng/

For more information, see BCIT International Students: https://www.bcit.ca/international-students/.

conditions.description: Scheduled intakes September each year. Application processing Full-time and part-time applications will be accepted as follows: First round: October 1st* to March 31st* Second round: April 1st* to April 30th* Third round: May 1st* to May 31st* Fourth round: June 1st* to July 31st* International applicants must hold a valid BCIT study permit to apply to the fourth round. *or next business day This program has multiple application deadlines and may fill after each deadline date. Entrance requirements Competitive Entry: Two-step process Step 1: Meet the following entrance requirements Upload proof of meeting the following requirements to your online application: English: one of the following: Two years of full-time post-secondary education in English in an English-speaking country with 3.0 credits of post-secondary English, humanities or social sciences (67%) from a recognized institution or View other ways to meet the English requirement Post-secondary: one of the following: A 4-year bachelor’s degree in an engineering field or architecture with a GPA of 2.8 out of 4.0 (70%) or A 4-year bachelor’s degree with a major in a related natural science field with a GPA of 2.8 out of 4.0 (70%), preferably with an Architectural and Building Technology (ABT) diploma (Building Science option) or equivalent building science industry experience. Your GPA will be calculated by using grades earned in the last two years of full-time study in the undergraduate degree. Applicants who have completed post-secondary studies outside of Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia or New Zealand will require a comprehensive evaluation of their credentials by the International Credential Evaluation Service (ICES) . Credential evaluation reports from other Canadian services may be considered. These reports must include course-by-course evaluations and GPA calculations. Math: Linear algebra and differential equations equivalent to UBC Math 221 and UBC Math 255. You are not required to take these specific UBC courses; they are listed here for you to refer to their course descriptions. If you have already studied these subjects as part of your bachelor’s degree, please give particulars in your online application: UBC Math 221 Matrix Algebra UBC Math 255 Ordinary Differential Equations Complete the following form for submission with your online application: Mandatory Applicant Questionnaire [PDF] : This form will be used with other entrance requirements in the competitive selection for the program. You will be required to provide two academic or professional references supporting your academic suitability. Step 2: Department Review Only complete applications that include all the required supporting documentation will be evaluated. All complete applications will be reviewed by the Graduate Selection Committee and ranked on a competitive basis. The applicants that are best suited for success in the program will be offered a place. Building envelope laboratory course Applicants without industry experience in building science may be required to enroll in BLDC 3060 - Building Envelope Laboratory. Fees for this course will need to be paid in addition to the master’s degree tuition. Applicants will be advised if they need to take this course after their application has been reviewed by the Graduate Selection Committee. Applicants who are required to take this course can do so concurrently with their first term studies. It is not necessary to complete this course prior to enrolling in the master’s program. Industry practitioners Industry practitioners are encouraged to apply for part-time study. Professional development Subject to departmental approval and course availability, students who satisfy the entrance requirements may take no more than two courses for professional development without first applying to the program. Please see Program details . International applicants The full-time option is available to international applicants. The part-time option is not available to international applicants. View available programs . Study permit: A valid BCIT study permit is required prior to starting the full-time program. Post-graduation Work Permit (PGWP) eligibility : Only the full-time option of this program currently meets the PGWP eligibility requirements based on study program - graduates with a master's degree and is eligible for students to apply for a PGWP. There are no field of study requirements (CIP) for graduates with a master’s degree. Students are responsible for meeting all Immigration, Refugees, and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) PGWP eligibility requirements . Final PGWP approval is at the discretion of IRCC. Transfer credit Transfer of credits is allowed to a maximum of two courses taken outside of the Building Science graduate programs. These courses cannot have been used to satisfy the requirements of another credential, must have been taken within five years of admission to the current program, and must demonstrate a standing of a least 74%. Apply to program Note: The full-time September 2026 intake is now closed for new applications. Applications for the part-time September 2026 intake are currently being accepted. Applications for the September 2027 intake will be accepted starting October 1, 2026. To submit your application: Include proof of meeting all entrance requirements. Convert all transcripts and supporting documents to PDF files . Have a credit card ready to pay the application fee. Apply Now Learn more about how to apply myCommunication Within two business days of submitting your completed application, BCIT will send a message to your personal and myBCIT email addresses. All correspondence regarding your application will be posted to your online myCommunication account at my.bcit.ca . We will send you an email when a new message is posted. It is important to watch for these emails or regularly check your account online. You can expect to receive communication concerning the status of your application within four weeks. Go back Overview Next up Costs & Supplies

program.program_overview: Note: The full-time September 2026 intake is now closed for new applications. Applications for the part-time September 2026 intake are currently being accepted. Applications for the September 2027 intake will be accepted starting October 1, 2026. Delivery: in person. See details . The Master of Engineering in Building Science degree is designed to provide students from various engineering disciplines with advanced knowledge and skills to achieve a holistic understanding of building performance through a core course component, which is composed of a fundamental technical cluster, and an applied technical cluster. Students will gain in-depth knowledge of a specialty area through focused elective technical courses or a supervised research project. The Master of Engineering degree: Offers an interdisciplinary curriculum Specializes in building science Emphasizes an engineering approach for practical problem solving Focuses on applied research to provide solutions to industry problems Engages students in interdisciplinary research Is supported by a strong foundation of research infrastructure unique to western Canada Delivers a first-of-a-kind program in BC and western Canada Program pathways MEng students are required to select one of two pathways for the completion of the program. Path 1: course option Students take 10 courses: 4 core courses and 6 elective courses. For this path the Research Methods course is optional. Except for the core fundamental courses, all other courses include a research component. Path 2: industry/research project option Students take 7 courses plus Research Methods, and a comprehensive industry/research project. Students engage in applied research on a relevant industry problem under the supervision of a faculty member. Acceptance into Path 2 is dependent on: A faculty supervisor accepting to supervise the student. The skills and motivation of the student to engage in applied research on a topic of interest for both student and supervisor. Students not accepted for Path 2 are enrolled in Path 1. Graduate student funding opportunities There is funding available on a competitive basis to graduate students. Please see the list of faculty members for their research interests and then contact the faculty individually if you would like more information. Next up Entrance Requirements

conditions.description: Scheduled intakes September each year. Application processing Full-time and part-time applications will be accepted as follows: First round: October 1st* to March 31st* Second round: April 1st* to April 30th* Third round: May 1st* to May 31st* Fourth round: June 1st* to July 31st* International applicants must hold a valid BCIT study permit to apply to the fourth round. *or next business day This program has multiple application deadlines and may fill after each deadline date. Entrance requirements Competitive Entry: Two-step process Step 1: Meet the following entrance requirements Upload proof of meeting the following requirements to your online application: English: one of the following: Two years of full-time post-secondary education in English in an English-speaking country with 3.0 credits of post-secondary English, humanities or social sciences (67%) from a recognized institution or View other ways to meet the English requirement Post-secondary: one of the following: A 4-year bachelor’s degree in an engineering field or architecture with a GPA of 2.8 out of 4.0 (70%) or A 4-year bachelor’s degree with a major in a related natural science field with a GPA of 2.8 out of 4.0 (70%), preferably with an Architectural and Building Technology (ABT) diploma (Building Science option) or equivalent building science industry experience. Your GPA will be calculated by using grades earned in the last two years of full-time study in the undergraduate degree. Applicants who have completed post-secondary studies outside of Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia or New Zealand will require a comprehensive evaluation of their credentials by the International Credential Evaluation Service (ICES) . Credential evaluation reports from other Canadian services may be considered. These reports must include course-by-course evaluations and GPA calculations. Math: Linear algebra and differential equations equivalent to UBC Math 221 and UBC Math 255. You are not required to take these specific UBC courses; they are listed here for you to refer to their course descriptions. If you have already studied these subjects as part of your bachelor’s degree, please give particulars in your online application: UBC Math 221 Matrix Algebra UBC Math 255 Ordinary Differential Equations Complete the following form for submission with your online application: Mandatory Applicant Questionnaire [PDF] : This form will be used with other entrance requirements in the competitive selection for the program. You will be required to provide two academic or professional references supporting your academic suitability. Step 2: Department Review Only complete applications that include all the required supporting documentation will be evaluated. All complete applications will be reviewed by the Graduate Selection Committee and ranked on a competitive basis. The applicants that are best suited for success in the program will be offered a place. Building envelope laboratory course Applicants without industry experience in building science may be required to enroll in BLDC 3060 - Building Envelope Laboratory. Fees for this course will need to be paid in addition to the master’s degree tuition. Applicants will be advised if they need to take this course after their application has been reviewed by the Graduate Selection Committee. Applicants who are required to take this course can do so concurrently with their first term studies. It is not necessary to complete this course prior to enrolling in the master’s program. Industry practitioners Industry practitioners are encouraged to apply for part-time study. Professional development Subject to departmental approval and course availability, students who satisfy the entrance requirements may take no more than two courses for professional development without first applying to the program. Please see Program details . International applicants The full-time option is available to international applicants. The part-time option is not available to international applicants. View available programs . Study permit: A valid BCIT study permit is required prior to starting the full-time program. Post-graduation Work Permit (PGWP) eligibility : Only the full-time option of this program currently meets the PGWP eligibility requirements based on study program - graduates with a master's degree and is eligible for students to apply for a PGWP. There are no field of study requirements (CIP) for graduates with a master’s degree. Students are responsible for meeting all Immigration, Refugees, and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) PGWP eligibility requirements . Final PGWP approval is at the discretion of IRCC. Transfer credit Transfer of credits is allowed to a maximum of two courses taken outside of the Building Science graduate programs. These courses cannot have been used to satisfy the requirements of another credential, must have been taken within five years of admission to the current program, and must demonstrate a standing of a least 74%. Apply to program Note: The full-time September 2026 intake is now closed for new applications. Applications for the part-time September 2026 intake are currently being accepted. Applications for the September 2027 intake will be accepted starting October 1, 2026. To submit your application: Include proof of meeting all entrance requirements. Convert all transcripts and supporting documents to PDF files . Have a credit card ready to pay the application fee. Apply Now Learn more about how to apply myCommunication Within two business days of submitting your completed application, BCIT will send a message to your personal and myBCIT email addresses. All correspondence regarding your application will be posted to your online myCommunication account at my.bcit.ca . We will send you an email when a new message is posted. It is important to watch for these emails or regularly check your account online. You can expect to receive communication concerning the status of your application within four weeks. Applications for the September 2027 intake will be accepted starting October 1, 2026. Delivery: in person. See details . The Master of Engineering in Building Science degree is designed to provide students from various engineering disciplines with advanced knowledge and skills to achieve a holistic understanding of building performance through a core course component, which is composed of a fundamental technical cluster, and an applied technical cluster. Students will gain in-depth knowledge of a specialty area through focused elective technical courses or a supervised research project. The Master of Engineering degree: Offers an interdisciplinary curriculum Specializes in building science Emphasizes an engineering approach for practical problem solving Focuses on applied research to provide solutions to industry problems Engages students in interdisciplinary research Is supported by a strong foundation of research infrastructure unique to western Canada Delivers a first-of-a-kind program in BC and western Canada Program pathways MEng students are required to select one of two pathways for the completion of the program. Path 1: course option Students take 10 courses: 4 core courses and 6 elective courses. For this path the Research Methods course is optional. Except for the core fundamental courses, all other courses include a research component. Path 2: industry/research project option Students take 7 courses plus Research Methods, and a comprehensive industry/research project. Students engage in applied research on a relevant industry problem under the supervision of a faculty member. Acceptance into Path 2 is dependent on: A faculty supervisor accepting to supervise the student. The skills and motivation of the student to engage in applied research on a topic of interest for both student and supervisor. Students not accepted for Path 2 are enrolled in Path 1. Graduate student funding opportunities There is funding available on a competitive basis to graduate students. Please see the list of faculty members for their research interests and then contact the faculty individually if you would like more information. Next up Entrance Requirements

Step 2: Department Review Only complete applications that include all the required supporting documentation will be evaluated. All complete applications will be reviewed by the Graduate Selection Committee and ranked on a competitive basis. The applicants that are best suited for success in the program will be offered a place. Industry practitioners Industry practitioners are encouraged to apply for part-time study. Professional development Subject to departmental approval and course availability, students who satisfy the entrance requirements may take no more than two courses for professional development without first applying to the program. Please see Program details . International applicants The full-time option is available to international applicants. The part-time option is not available to international applicants. View available programs . Study permit: A valid BCIT study permit is required prior to starting the full-time program. There are no field of study requirements (CIP) for graduates with a master\u2019s degree. Students are responsible for meeting all Immigration, Refugees, and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) PGWP eligibility requirements . Final PGWP approval is at the discretion of IRCC. Transfer credit Transfer of credits is allowed to a maximum of two courses taken outside of the Building Science graduate programs. These courses cannot have been used to satisfy the requirements of another credential, must have been taken within five years of admission to the current program, and must demonstrate a standing of a least 74%. ## What I can verify from the Asteris program record

For BCIT’s **Building Science Master of Engineering**:

- It is an active **Master of Engineering** program delivered at the Burnaby Campus.
- The program has full-time and part-time study modes, but the stored admission rules state that **international applicants may apply to the full-time option only**.
- A valid BCIT study permit is required before starting the full-time program.
- Admission is competitive. Meeting the stated entrance requirements does **not** guarantee admission; complete applications are reviewed and ranked by the Graduate Selection Committee.
- The stored entrance requirements include:
  - An accepted English-language qualification
  - A qualifying four-year degree and the stated GPA standard
  - Linear algebra and differential equations equivalent to the specified mathematics background
  - A completed applicant questionnaire
  - Two academic or professional references
  - Required supporting documentation, including credential evaluation where applicable
- Applicants without building-science industry experience **may be required** to take a building-envelope laboratory course. The department decides this after reviewing the application.
- The program record states that application-status communication should be provided through **myCommunication/myBCIT**, with status communication expected within four weeks after a completed application.
- The program record states that only the full-time option currently meets the program-based conditions for applying for a post-graduation work permit; final eligibility is determined by IRCC.
- The curriculum includes required core technical coursework, technical electives, graduate seminars, and either a course-based pathway or an industry/research-project pathway. The project pathway requires faculty-supervisor acceptance.

The stored record also says that the **full-time September 2026 intake is closed** and that applications for **September 2027** are scheduled to open on **October 1, 2026**. Because intake dates and availability can change, this should be reconfirmed with BCIT.

## What I cannot verify about you

I cannot verify:

- Whether your application has been submitted or is complete
- Whether your documents satisfy BCIT’s requirements
- Whether your degree, GPA, English evidence, mathematics background, or references have been accepted
- Whether you need the building-envelope laboratory course
- Whether the Graduate Selection Committee has selected you
- Whether you have been admitted
- Whether your study permit will be issued
- Whether you personally qualify for a future PGWP

## What you should confirm directly with BCIT

Ask BCIT Admissions or the program contact to confirm:

1. Your current application status in **myCommunication/myBCIT**
2. Whether all required documents have been received and accepted
3. Whether your international credentials require an ICES evaluation
4. Whether your academic background satisfies the mathematics and degree requirements
5. Whether you need the building-envelope laboratory course
6. Whether the relevant intake is still accepting applications and whether deadlines or round availability have changed
7. The official admission decision and any conditions attached to an offer
8. Study-permit and immigration requirements for your specific situation
9. Your individual PGWP eligibility, with IRCC if necessary

program.program_overview: Note: The full-time September 2026 intake is now closed for new applications. Applications for the part-time September 2026 intake are currently being accepted. Applications for the September 2027 intake will be accepted starting October 1, 2026. Delivery: in person. See details . The Master of Engineering in Building Science degree is designed to provide students from various engineering disciplines with advanced knowledge and skills to achieve a holistic understanding of building performance through a core course component, which is composed of a fundamental technical cluster, and an applied technical cluster. Students will gain in-depth knowledge of a specialty area through focused elective technical courses or a supervised research project. The Master of Engineering degree: Offers an interdisciplinary curriculum Specializes in building science Emphasizes an engineering approach for practical problem solving Focuses on applied research to provide solutions to industry problems Engages students in interdisciplinary research Is supported by a strong foundation of research infrastructure unique to western Canada Delivers a first-of-a-kind program in BC and western Canada Program pathways MEng students are required to select one of two pathways for the completion of the program. Path 1: course option Students take 10 courses: 4 core courses and 6 elective courses. For this path the Research Methods course is optional. Except for the core fundamental courses, all other courses include a research component. Path 2: industry/research project option Students take 7 courses plus Research Methods, and a comprehensive industry/research project. Students engage in applied research on a relevant industry problem under the supervision of a faculty member. Acceptance into Path 2 is dependent on: A faculty supervisor accepting to supervise the student. The skills and motivation of the student to engage in applied research on a topic of interest for both student and supervisor. Students not accepted for Path 2 are enrolled in Path 1. Graduate student funding opportunities There is funding available on a competitive basis to graduate students. Please see the list of faculty members for their research interests and then contact the faculty individually if you would like more information. Next up Entrance Requirements

## What I can verify from the Asteris program record

For BCIT’s **Building Science Master of Engineering**:

- It is an active **Master of Engineering** program delivered at the Burnaby Campus.
- The program has full-time and part-time study modes, but the stored admission rules state that **international applicants may apply to the full-time option only**.
- A valid BCIT study permit is required before starting the full-time program.
- Admission is competitive. Meeting the stated entrance requirements does **not** guarantee admission; complete applications are reviewed and ranked by the Graduate Selection Committee.
- The stored entrance requirements include:
  - An accepted English-language qualification
  - A qualifying four-year degree and the stated GPA standard
  - Linear algebra and differential equations equivalent to the specified mathematics background
  - A completed applicant questionnaire
  - Two academic or professional references
  - Required supporting documentation, including credential evaluation where applicable
- Applicants without building-science industry experience **may be required** to take a building-envelope laboratory course. The department decides this after reviewing the application.
- The program record states that application-status communication should be provided through **myCommunication/myBCIT**, with status communication expected within four weeks after a completed application.
- The program record states that only the full-time option currently meets the program-based conditions for applying for a post-graduation work permit; final eligibility is determined by IRCC.
- The curriculum includes required core technical coursework, technical electives, graduate seminars, and either a course-based pathway or an industry/research-project pathway. The project pathway requires faculty-supervisor acceptance.

The stored record also says that the **full-time September 2026 intake is closed** and that applications for **September 2027** are scheduled to open on **October 1, 2026**. Because intake dates and availability can change, this should be reconfirmed with BCIT.

## What I cannot verify about you

I cannot verify:

- Whether your application has been submitted or is complete
- Whether your documents satisfy BCIT’s requirements
- Whether your degree, GPA, English evidence, mathematics background, or references have been accepted
- Whether you need the building-envelope laboratory course
- Whether the Graduate Selection Committee has selected you
- Whether you have been admitted
- Whether your study permit will be issued
- Whether you personally qualify for a future PGWP

## What you should confirm directly with BCIT

Ask BCIT Admissions or the program contact to confirm:

1. Your current application status in **myCommunication/myBCIT**
2. Whether all required documents have been received and accepted
3. Whether your international credentials require an ICES evaluation
4. Whether your academic background satisfies the mathematics and degree requirements
5. Whether you need the building-envelope laboratory course
6. Whether the relevant intake is still accepting applications and whether deadlines or round availability have changed
7. The official admission decision and any conditions attached to an offer
8. Study-permit and immigration requirements for your specific situation
9. Your individual PGWP eligibility, with IRCC if necessary
